parts.text: As more terms in these sequences of fractions are calculated the difference between the terms becomes smaller and smaller. This means that the terms become nearly equal to the same number. This number is called the limit of the sequence.

content.tex: As more terms in these sequences of fractions are calculated the difference between the terms becomes smaller and smaller. This means that the terms become nearly equal to the same number. This number is called the limit of the sequence.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) In the sequence in question 1 all the terms after the 7th term are the same when written correct to 3 decimal places. If x is a fraction in the sequence in question 1 then the next fraction is x + 1 1 . In this case the sequence reaches its limit when x x + = 1 1 .

content.tex: In the sequence in question 1 all the terms after the 7th term are the same when written correct to 3 decimal places. If \(x\) is a fraction in the sequence in question 1 then the next fraction is \(\frac{1}{1+ x}\) .
In this case the sequence reaches its limit when \(x = \frac{1}{1+ x}\) .

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Show that x x + = 1 1 can be rearranged to give the quadratic equation x 2 + x − 1 = 0.

content.tex: Show that \(x = \frac{1}{1+ x}\) can be rearranged to give the quadratic equation \(x^{2} + x - 1 = 0.\)
